seo.title: Work Agent for Recruiters and Hiring Teams | Floatboat
seo.description: A Work Agent for recruiters that turns approved hiring inputs into role briefs, candidate evidence packets, interview plans, and review-ready communications.

hero.eyebrow: A Work Agent for responsible hiring preparation
hero.title: A Work Agent for recruiters and talent teams
hero.description: Give Floatboat an approved role brief, candidate materials, and interview standards. It prepares evidence packets, interview plans, feedback summaries, and communication drafts for recruiter review.

burdens.eyebrow: Where a recruiting Work Agent earns its place
burdens.title: Keep hiring judgment with people. Give the preparation work to an agent.
burdens.description: Hiring slows down when the role, evidence, interview criteria, and candidate communication are rebuilt by different people at every stage.

items.label: Context
items.title: Job requirements begin ambiguous
items.description: A job title can hide conflicting expectations about outcomes, seniority, constraints, and what success should look like.

items.label: Format
items.title: Candidate context is repeatedly reconstructed
items.description: Recruiters and interviewers repeatedly turn résumés, notes, portfolios, and correspondence into their own partial summaries.

items.label: Coordination
items.title: Interview evidence arrives in different formats
items.description: Scorecards, free-form notes, and delayed feedback make it difficult to compare evidence against the agreed role criteria.

items.label: Continuity
items.title: Status communication consumes focus
items.description: Scheduling changes, interviewer reminders, candidate updates, and debrief follow-ups compete with actual recruiting judgment.

buildingBlocks.eyebrow: What your recruiting Work Agent can prepare
buildingBlocks.title: Move from approved hiring inputs to review-ready materials.
buildingBlocks.description: The Work Agent uses the workspace to keep role criteria, candidate evidence, interview notes, and deliverables connected while your team controls every consequential decision.

items.example: Read the approved role brief, candidate submissions, correspondence, and interview rubric.
Arrange evidence by role criterion, interview stage, and source.
Pull candidate-provided evidence and mark unanswered role questions.
Map each packet against the same approved, job-related criteria without ranking people.
Draft interviewer briefs, debrief summaries, and candidate updates.
Reuse proven packet formats and approval gates for the next search.

workflows.eyebrow: Three assignments for a recruiting Work Agent
workflows.title: Delegate the preparation around a hiring decision—not the decision itself.
workflows.description: Each assignment starts from approved, job-related material, returns an inspectable deliverable, and stops before candidate evaluation or outreach.

items.title: Turn intake into a role brief
items.job: Consolidate business need, outcomes, constraints, and interview criteria before sourcing begins.
items.output: A shared role brief and structured scorecard draft.
items.boundary: The hiring team sets lawful criteria and approves the role requirements.

items.title: Prepare a candidate evidence packet
items.job: Organize candidate-provided material against approved, job-related criteria for human review.
items.output: A source-linked packet with evidence and interview questions.
items.boundary: People—not the system—assess candidates and make employment decisions.

items.title: Coordinate interviews and follow-up
items.job: Create interviewer briefs, consolidate notes, and draft timely candidate communications.
items.output: Interview packs, debrief summary, and editable status messages.
items.boundary: Recruiters approve communications and protect sensitive candidate information.

customization.title: Teach the Work Agent how your hiring team prepares.
customization.description: Give it your lawful criteria, interview rubric, packet format, terminology, and approval path; keep candidate judgment with accountable people.
controls: What the agent may read or change
What must never be sent automatically
What can be saved and shared

progression.eyebrow: From one assignment to a reusable Work Agent
progression.title: Prove the Work Agent on one hiring deliverable before expanding its role.
progression.description: A recruiting routine should expand only after recruiters confirm that its packets are accurate, job-related, and useful to interviewers.

items.label: Ad hoc
items.title: Prepare one interviewer packet
items.description: Use one approved role brief and one candidate's submitted materials to prepare a source-linked packet for recruiter review.

items.label: Saved workflow
items.title: Reuse the packet method for the search
items.description: Keep the same job-related criteria, evidence labels, missing-information rules, and recruiter approval gate for later candidates.

items.label: Team practice
items.title: Standardize preparation across the hiring team
items.description: Give recruiters and interviewers a consistent briefing format while each evaluator records their own evidence and remains accountable for judgment.

boundaries.title: Let the Work Agent prepare evidence. Keep employment decisions human.
boundaries.description: The Work Agent may organize job-related evidence and draft materials; it must not infer protected traits, rank people, reject applicants, or make employment decisions.
boundaries.assistsTitle: The Work Agent can help prepare
assists: Role briefs that separate required outcomes from unresolved hiring-manager requests
Source-linked candidate evidence mapped to approved, job-related criteria
Interviewer packets with focused questions and clearly marked information gaps
Debrief summaries that preserve who supplied each observation
Candidate-status messages held as drafts until a recruiter approves them
retains: Defining lawful role criteria and deciding which evidence is relevant
Evaluating candidates, investigating gaps, and making employment decisions
Preventing protected or unnecessary sensitive attributes from entering the process
Choosing interview panels, stages, compensation ranges, and hiring priorities
Approving every candidate-facing message, disposition, offer, or rejection
boundaries.note: Floatboat is a general-purpose Work Agent, not an ATS or hiring authority. Its workspace keeps approved files, tools, instructions, and deliverables together; data handling depends on the models, connectors, permissions, and policies you select.

faq.title: Work Agent questions for recruiters and talent teams
faq.description: Recruiting automation must improve preparation without turning incomplete evidence into a hiring decision or weakening candidate privacy.

items.question: Is Floatboat an ATS or candidate-ranking system?
items.answer: No. Your ATS remains the hiring system of record. Floatboat helps prepare role briefs, interview materials, evidence summaries, and communication drafts around the information your team is permitted to use.

items.question: Can it screen out or rank candidates automatically?
items.answer: That is not the intended workflow. It can organize job-related evidence against approved criteria, but recruiters and hiring managers must evaluate people, investigate gaps, and make employment decisions.

items.question: Can it use our role brief and interview scorecard?
items.answer: Yes. Define outcomes, required evidence, legal constraints, question areas, and the scorecard format before candidate preparation begins.

items.question: How do we prevent invented candidate claims?
items.answer: Limit summaries to candidate-provided or approved sources, preserve links to the original evidence, label missing information as unknown, and require a recruiter to verify every claim used in an interview brief.

items.question: What candidate information belongs in the workspace?
items.answer: Only job-relevant information that policy and applicable law permit the team to process. Keep the Work Agent workspace limited to necessary files, avoid unnecessary sensitive attributes, and review each model and connector's data practices.

items.question: Can it contact candidates or schedule interviews without review?
items.answer: It can prepare messages and scheduling options, but a responsible recruiter should confirm recipients, availability, wording, and stage before any candidate-facing action.

items.question: What is the safest first recruiting workflow?
items.answer: Start with an approved role brief and scorecard, then generate an interviewer packet for one candidate. Check every statement against the source material before deciding whether to reuse the process.

finalCta.title: Make the interview packet evidence-led
finalCta.description: Bring the approved role brief and candidate materials. Prepare structured questions and evidence notes; people make the hiring call.
